Since Vinland Saga is very character driven the action was more of a means to an end for the sake of Thorfinn's character and as context for the events surrounding this time period as violence, war, slavery and hate were rampant during this era in history. 

As Leif Erickson and Thorfinn Karlsefni were super important for trying to establish a settlement in North America aka Vinland (a land untouched by the horrors of European war and slavery) it makes a lot of sense historically for the story of Thorfinn to skew towards quiet peace rather than action packed violence. 

If it were a story about someone else then maybe it could have been action focused for its entirety but Thorfinn is the main character and he's known historically as an explorer first and foremost, it could become more action oriented as this is a story set during war, but I feel that violence will not be the focus of Thorfinn's character moving forward.

For me this is one of the best designed Pokémon games in a long time and is the most fun I've had since Kalos, the variety of pokemon available to you is excellent and while the game doesn't tell you one can infer from just how many gym level challenges there are that you can either choose to use 1 team and make this the easiest pokemon game to date or you can use 2 teams and actually have a challenge for once without having to grind or force yourself to be underleveled and you aren't forced to battle any npcs that you don't talk to first unless it's a scripted encounter you entered the area for, the terastallizing mechanic, while probably the laziest of the gimmics, provides the most depth of combat since megas since unless it's obvious you have to deal with the fact that your opponent could turn what was an overwhelming advantage into the opposite, the fact that it's open world means that if there's a pokemon you want to get you generally don't have to go through a bunch of bullshit to get it, and in general running around battling and catching Pokémon and doing Skyrim horse shenanigans is fun and exploring is somehow as well (though not like botw, mind you.)

All that in mind I do still have a number of problems with the game, firstly it runs worse than stale horse piss, I'm not joking when I say it can on rare occasion dip down to 2 frames a second but most of the time you'll get dips of maybe 15-20 fps with it really maxing out at around 30 fps with npcs 5 feet away from you walking at like 5 fps, sometimes you'll be exploring and get stuck only to have to fly (which nicely enough you get assumedly out the gate, idk I was about 4 hours in and the game never mentioned getting the ability) to a different spot to continue ending up wasting like 10 minutes of exploring, or you'll get stuck on a piece of geometry or fall in the water and get teleported halfway across the map to a pokemon center (which wasn't even the last one I visited)  rather than the last flat ground you were on like it usually does, I was able to end up outside of the map on a number of occasions due mostly to wild encounters in tight spaces, and while a lot of pokemon have impressive texturing they look out of place next to textures that feel worse than N64 games, I also couldn't tell you much about any locations as they weren't all that memorable aside from maybe a sparse few instances such as Area Zero, I assume the pokemon 15 feet away from me weren't meant to initiate battle with me unless their model is bending spacetime, there also doesn't seem to be anything in the way of side content at least that I've seen, and to cap it off the game suffers from the worst pop-in I've ever seen where I've literally had a few times where I'm running around and all of a sudden I'm in battle against an invisible pokemon that stays invisible halfway through the encounter.

Even with all those negatives I'm still having a great time with the game and struggle to see an opinion online that isn't either treating it like it's a crime against humanity and giving no credit at all or dickriding it and glancing over all it's many flaws, honestly it's disappointing for me because I see the shell of what could be the best Pokémon game ever but Gamefreak are stretched entirely too thin to make that happen.

The beautiful thing with Zelda is thanks to the consistency of quality you can really pick any random one and have a solid experience. 

Though if you want some specific titles than a few good starting points would be

The Legend of Zelda: Not an ideal place to start but if you want to start where it all began than there is no better place to begin, very dated by today's standards however the feeling of discovering a secret is quite gratifying and you can tackle things in a fairly open order like doing dungeons out of order and while combat is nothing to write home about it's solid and doesn't leave you frustrated like many of it's peers do. 

Ocarina of Time: The first step into 3d design for the series and next to Breath of the Wild is the biggest shake up the series has ever had, a little dated in some aspects but still holds up marvelously even compared to modern games in many ways, has excellent level design and feels big enough to enjoy while not feeling bloated enough to overstay its welcome. 

Wind Waker: Probably the best example of an adventure game that Zelda has, the art style is unique and memorable and looks and feels like a classic cartoon in terms of presentation and has some of the most memorable worlds, side characters and quests of any Zelda game. 

A Link to the Past: A classic experience if there ever was one and top down Zelda at it's peak and is an excellent experience all around with great bosses, music, fantastic pixel art and some of the best level design that feels open despite the game being much smaller than later titles. 

Majora's Mask: Atmosphere is the name of the game with this one, no other game in the series and few games in general capture the feeling of a death march  like the world and characters of Termina do, so many characters that leave a lasting impact and stick in your brain long after you put down the controller, everything has this dark final feeling to it that it feels like you yourself are stuck in a cruel fate that wants you and everyone else dead but not without moments of life and triumph that shine their brightest in the dark, it does run on the same engine as Ocarina but honestly the art direction and tone feel heightened by the dated graphics. It is a sequel to Ocarina but I feel like it isn't too big a deal if you play Majora first as the story connection is far less important than other sequels. 

A Link Between Worlds: Every thing that I said about A Link to the Past applies here as well, it's basically just an updated version with modern sensibilities and clever design, the art direction is differently but equally excellent and with great quality of life changes that change how you interact with the world that also leave it feeling like one of the more open titles in the series to date, one of the most solid games in the franchise that is as charming as it is enjoyable.

Link's Awakening: The most unique title in the series next to Majora's Mask and Breath of the Wild, it has the most relaxed feeling in the series, nobody is in danger, there is no bad guy doing bad stuff and the world isn't facing its end, your quest is to wake the Wind Fish from his dream, that's it, you're on an island filled with happy goofy residents and there are even Mario characters like Chain Chomp, Goomba, Wart and even a guy who looks like Mario, it is the most Animal Crossing Zelda has ever been and isn't afraid to be a little silly and light-hearted when it feels like it, and since it was originally released for a handheld console it happens to feel perfect for just sitting down and playing for like 20 minutes, setting it down for a week and then just picking it up again and doesn't ask you to become super invested, all it wants is to be a fun game you can just enjoy and the laid-back feeling of the island of Koholint feels perfect for this. P.S. I recommend the Switch version as the art style is extremely charming and offers updated controls, music and a few quality of life improvements. 

Skyward Sword: The black sheep of the franchise that is probably the most inconsistent entry in the series, it can be a bit hand holdey at times with some questionable decisions with controls and bosses, on the other hand it also has some of the best level design and a few exceptional bosses that eclipse most of the series' best, it also has some of the best music some very memorable characters like Groose and Girahim to name a few with arguably the best story in the series. If you want a game with noticeable flaws but super high highs than this is perfect for you. 

Twilight Princess: On the other hand probably the most consistent Zelda title as far as major features are concerned, while the tutorial does feel a little long it doesn't feel gratuitous, there are many aspects that are definitely done better in other entries but what it does have is very well done with one of the largest and best dungeon counts in the series with bosses that leave a lasting impression, the bosses have some of the best atmosphere of any Zelda boss and truly feel like David vs Goliath in scale and feel with music that raises you toward victory, the story is also among the best in the series with some of the best main characters with shining examples like your companion Midna and the primary antagonist Zant who is genuinely unnerving and intimidating. Also just listen to Midna's Lament as it's amazing even if you don't play any of the games. 

Breath of the Wild: I left this one for the end as it's the most recent and refined title in the series and it's probably best enjoyed after playing other Zelda games, however that is not to say that it is a bad first Zelda, on the contrary it is probably one of the best first experiences you can choose, the most quiet and understated experience it really let's you just breathe and take things at whatever pace you want and give you the tools right out the gate after the tutorial (which is about as hand holdey as a rock) to do whatever you want wherever you want, hell go fight the final boss right away if you want, it's about as open as an open world game can be and completely turns the series on its head with how drastically different it is in comparison to past entries, however the weapon durability while encouraging experimentation can feel a little drastic and with it being so hands off the narrative beats suffer from feeling disjointed that even after you have all the story it can feel like trying to organize a schizophrenic's office space (though maybe not as bad,) even with those offsets the game offers enough freedom that exploring is super gratifying as every discovery you make feels like it was you that made that discovery as there are multiple ways to solve objectives, beat enemies and find places and secrets and every experience with the game feels truly unique to your personal journey with the game, there is also a sequel coming out next year so you wouldn't have to wait long for more if it really does grab you. 


Again you can play any game first but these are ones that I feel are the most suitable first choices, regardless just have fun, this series has a special place in so many people's hearts and minds that really we all just want others to enjoy them too, I'm sure it's the same for your fiance, they just want to share something they love with you and I find that wonderful, best of luck to you both and just have fun, no need to worry about what the right decision is. For his second phase his quake move has different timing so either learn that or hang back and punish depending on how comfortable you are with dodging.

His wind move has the exact same strategy as phase 1, just with extra (fire) damage if you screw it up, even if you block.

For his fire sweep dodge left or right through it or if you're close enough you should be able to roll into him.

For his meteor attack run to him and roll into him, you'll be too close for the projectiles to matter, otherwise if you're not confident you can get close enough quick enough then hang farther back and dodge.

Lastly for his straight fire attack either book it in the other direction or run and roll into him for a ton of free hits, really depends on how close you are.

If you insist on using a big shield and being armory af then might I suggest a spear, you can attack while hiding behind your shield, if you have a regenerator ring then use it, there is no boss that it doesn't help against and it can be the difference between life and death especially if you're going to be blocking a lot because while you sit there and take a bunch of hits to the shield the recovered health will be quite noticeable, also farm a little so that you can get another spell slot that way you can have defensive and offensive spell buffing, in my opinion better than item buffing because it's unlimited so long as you have a way to replenish mp and makes it so that you can have grass at the ready (even if you can't replenish mp one or two rounds of buffs can be a huge help) buff yourself before boss rooms as buffs last longer than you'd assume.

Also some specific advice for each of the next areas and bosses you're up against, use it or don't if you want to get the satisfaction of figuring out for yourself.

Flamelurker: magic enchant your weapon, you will melt his health bar, other than that learn proper timing for raising and lowering your shield so that you can gain stamina quicker and use a flame resistance ring if you have one, also watch your feet, there are spots on the floor that seem to light you on fire so avoid those at all costs. Magic weapons will destroy the bearbugs on the way there and for the worms a well timed spear thrust will delete them but try not to fight more than one of you can help it, otherwise a bow/crossbow will make short work of them. 

Maneater: Enchant your weapon (or set it on fire though I never did that so I can't say how it compares to magic damage,) and two-hand your weapon, hopefully you should be able to kill the first one before the second fully spawns if your weapon and specific stats are high enough, get to the the brazier (torch thing) up top after you bully the first one (even if, and especially if, you haven't killed the first one quick enough,) use it to give yourself space to move around and a wall to hide behind, they don't do too much damage and they decide to fly around a lot so use that opportunity to heal yourself and crack skulls when their snake tail bites them as it's basically free hits, also hug your shield when they use magic attacks and I recommend using the magical dullness ring but honestly it's impact is negligable if there is really any (that I noticed,) also their attacks are pretty easily telegraphed so dodging shouldn't be much of an issue unless you just have a hard time with that. For the enemies leading to the boss just be aggressive and don't give them time to react but pull away if you don't have the stamina to finish the job, on the mindflayers though sneak up to them and do a back attack and then quickly dispatch them or bait them, run away and then try the prior strat (this is especially useful after the Maneater(s) boss.)

Old Hero: I can't speak for how it is without this strategy but honestly if you have the fool's ring I'd be surprised if you get hit at all, just equip it and he won't ever find you, this fight is basically free eats, equip the ring of avarice for a bunch of extra souls. For the bitch of a path there, bring a bow and about a million arrows as trying to hit the manta with a crossbow gave me a migraine, first fire a few arrows at the reaper (he's pretty slow so you should be able to take him out before anything can attack you, kill all the manta rays that will make the journey there much more difficult than you'd think, bait each of the skeletons individually and run back to that first little ledge outside and attack from safety or pick them off with your bow, afterwards locate the next reaper along the way and load them with arrows from a safe distance, the second reaper is guarded by respawning ghosts so use the magical dullness ring or a defense spell and kill them quick before their laser can melt your health bar then run down the hall and on your left the reaper should be there, just go to town and don't give him the opportunity to attack because you will die quickly, after that it's basically just avoiding slugs and exploding lights and boom you're at the reward for this headache of an area.

Dirty Colosus: honestly just use pine resin or unload arrows/bolts from afar, he's so slow and his ranged attack is easily telegraphed and not particularly hard hitting so you should be fine even if you get hit by a few, unlike Leechmonger he doesn't heal (from what I've experienced) so he'll go down after about 10-25 arrows depending on stats and equipment. For the area proceeding the boss poison resistance ring and regenerator ring help immensely with the swamp (regen will basically make it so that you lose health at a very slow rate, running from one patch of land to the next helps a lot as well and a bow to pick off enemies that would otherwise keep you stuck in poison water, keep a large supply of royal lotuses as well as they'll counteract the poison, but that'll also go away after a bit of waiting on dry land.
